declared.title: When failure fails to be productive: probing the effectiveness of productive failure for learning beyond STEM domains

population: 10th graders from 8 schools in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany (212 and 152 students), in a university lab, learning social science research methods

findings.text: Students who tried a problem before instruction did not learn social science methods better than students taught first, in either study

support.sentence: Thus, the findings did not replicate the PF effect on learning in a non-STEM domain.

findings.text: In Study 1, students who tried first scored lower than students taught first on application and transfer items (a medium-sized difference)

support.sentence: Contrary to our expectations, PF students achieved a significantly lower score than DI students (see Table 9).
support.readBy: failure-teaches writer, 2026-11-26: published version (Ruhr-Universität Bochum repository), Study 1 results

limits: quasi-experimental: whole classes assigned to a condition (Study 1: 6 classes vs 5), analysed per student
one domain (research methods), one age group, one out-of-school lab in Germany
Study 1 favoured instruction first (partial eta squared 0.12 on total learning, 0.13 on transfer); Study 2 found no significant difference
